explanation: The Church of England is the established Church in England. The monarch is its Supreme Governor and the Archbishop of Canterbury its spiritual leader.

angles.q: Which Church is the official Church of the state in England?
alts: What is the established Church in England?
England's state Church is which of these?

angles.q: Who is the Supreme Governor of the Church of England?
alts: Who heads the Church of England?

tf.s: The Archbishop of Canterbury is the spiritual leader of the Church of England.
The Church of England is also known as the Anglican Church.

explanation: The Church of Scotland is a Presbyterian Church, governed by ministers and elders, whose chair is the Moderator, appointed for one year.

angles.q: Who chairs the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland?
alts: The General Assembly of the Church of Scotland is chaired by whom?

tf.s: The Moderator of the Church of Scotland is appointed for one year.
The Church of Scotland is governed by ministers and elders.

explanation: The UK is a diverse society. People of many religions live and worship freely, and everyone has the right to have no religion.

tf.s: Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs, Jews and Buddhists all worship freely in the UK.
It is compulsory to belong to a religion in the UK.
A growing proportion of people in the UK report having no religion.

explanation: Lent lasts 40 days before Easter, beginning on Ash Wednesday. Good Friday marks the death of Jesus and Easter Sunday his resurrection.

angles.q: How many days does Lent last?
alts: Lent is a period of how many days?
The fasting period before Easter lasts how long?

angles.q: Which day is the day before Lent begins?
alts: Pancake Day is another name for which day?

tf.s: Good Friday marks the death of Jesus Christ.
Easter Monday is a public holiday in Scotland.

explanation: Bonfire Night on 5 November recalls the Gunpowder Plot of 1605, when Guy Fawkes and others tried to blow up Parliament.

angles.q: Which event is remembered on 5 November?
wrong: The end of the First World War
alts: Bonfire Night commemorates what?
What failed plot is remembered each 5 November?

tf.s: Fireworks and bonfires are traditional on 5 November.

explanation: Remembrance Day on 11 November commemorates those who died in war. A two-minute silence is held at 11am and poppies are worn.

angles.q: How long is the silence held on Remembrance Day?
alts: A silence of what length is observed on Remembrance Day?

tf.s: The two-minute silence on Remembrance Day is held at 11am.
Remembrance Day commemorates those who died fighting for the UK and its allies.

explanation: Traditional foods include roast beef and Yorkshire pudding in England, haggis in Scotland, Welsh cakes in Wales and the Ulster fry in Northern Ireland.

angles.q: The Ulster fry is a traditional dish from which part of the UK?
alts: Which country of the UK is the Ulster fry associated with?

angles.q: Welsh cakes are a traditional dish from which country?
alts: Which part of the UK is known for Welsh cakes?

multi.q: Which TWO of these are traditional Scottish foods?

explanation: Football is the most popular sport in the UK, with professional leagues in all four countries.

angles.q: Which is the most popular spectator sport in the UK?
alts: What is the UK's best-supported sport?
Which sport attracts the largest following in the UK?

tf.s: There are professional football leagues in all four countries of the UK.
England won the football World Cup in 1966.

explanation: Cricket originated in England. Lord's in London is regarded as the home of cricket, and test matches can last five days.

angles.q: Which London ground is known as the home of cricket?
alts: Cricket's most famous ground in London is which?

tf.s: Twenty20 is a shorter form of cricket played in a single day.

explanation: Rugby originated in England. There are two forms, union and league, and rugby league began in the north of England.

angles.q: What are the two main forms of rugby?
alts: Rugby is played in which two codes?

tf.s: The Six Nations is an annual rugby union competition.
Twickenham is the home of English rugby union.

explanation: London hosted the Olympics in 1908, 1948 and 2012. The Paralympics grew from competitions at Stoke Mandeville Hospital.

angles.q: Which British hospital gave rise to the Paralympic Games?
alts: The Paralympic movement began at which hospital?

tf.s: London was the first city to host the modern Olympics three times.

explanation: The Brit Awards recognise popular music and the Mercury Music Prize is awarded for the best album from the UK and Ireland.

angles.q: Which awards recognise achievement in British popular music?
alts: The annual awards for UK popular music are called what?

tf.s: The Mercury Music Prize is awarded for the best album from the UK and Ireland.
The Brit Awards are given for achievement in film.

explanation: British composers include Henry Purcell, Sir Edward Elgar, Gustav Holst, Ralph Vaughan Williams and Benjamin Britten.

angles.q: Which of these is a well-known British composer?
alts: Which of these composers was British?

tf.s: Gustav Holst composed The Planets.
Henry Purcell was an organist at Westminster Abbey.

explanation: The Laurence Olivier Awards recognise achievement in London theatre, and the Edinburgh Festival includes the Fringe.

angles.q: The Laurence Olivier Awards are given for excellence in what?
alts: Which field do the Olivier Awards recognise?

tf.s: The Edinburgh Festival takes place every summer.
Pantomime is traditionally performed at Christmas.

explanation: The Booker Prize is awarded annually for fiction, and the Turner Prize for contemporary art.

angles.q: Which prize is awarded annually for the best novel?
alts: The leading UK award for fiction is which prize?

explanation: Famous British authors include Shakespeare, Chaucer, Austen, Dickens, the Brontes, Hardy, Orwell and Conan Doyle.

angles.q: Which author wrote Great Expectations?
alts: Great Expectations was written by whom?

angles.q: Which author wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four?
alts: Nineteen Eighty-Four is the work of which writer?

multi.q: Which TWO of these were written by Jane Austen?

explanation: Robert Burns is the national poet of Scotland, and Dylan Thomas was a Welsh poet. William Wordsworth was one of the Romantic poets.

angles.q: Who is known as the national poet of Scotland?
alts: Scotland's national poet is who?
Which poet is celebrated each 25 January in Scotland?

tf.s: Auld Lang Syne was written by Robert Burns.
Poets' Corner is in Westminster Abbey.

explanation: Notable British architects include Sir Christopher Wren, Robert Adam, John Nash, Sir Charles Barry and Sir Norman Foster.

angles.q: Who designed the Houses of Parliament?
alts: The Houses of Parliament were designed by which architect?

tf.s: Sir Christopher Wren rebuilt St Paul's Cathedral after the Great Fire.
John Nash designed Buckingham Palace.

explanation: British cinema includes Ealing comedies, the films of Sir Alfred Hitchcock and Sir Charlie Chaplin, and the James Bond series.

angles.q: Which British director is famous for films including Psycho and The Birds?
alts: Psycho and The Birds were directed by whom?

tf.s: Sir Charlie Chaplin became famous in silent films.
The James Bond films are based on novels by Ian Fleming.

explanation: A television licence is required for each household that watches or records live TV, and it funds the BBC.

angles.q: What funds the BBC?
alts: The BBC's main source of income is what?

tf.s: It is a criminal offence to watch live television without a licence.
The BBC is independent of government.

explanation: Popular pastimes in the UK include gardening, shopping, cooking, sport and going to the pub.

angles.q: What is an allotment used for?
alts: People rent allotments in order to do what?

tf.s: You normally have to be 18 to buy alcohol in a UK pub.
Gardening is a popular pastime in the UK.

explanation: UK landmarks include Big Ben, the Tower of London, Edinburgh Castle, the Giant's Causeway, Snowdonia and the Eden Project.

angles.q: Where is Edinburgh Castle?
alts: Edinburgh Castle stands in which country of the UK?

angles.q: In which country of the UK is Snowdonia National Park?
alts: Snowdonia is found in which part of the UK?

tf.s: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell at the Houses of Parliament.
The Eden Project is in Cornwall.
Loch Lomond is in Wales.

explanation: The National Trust, founded in 1895, is a charity that preserves important buildings, coastline and countryside.

angles.q: In which year was the National Trust founded?
alts: The National Trust was established in which year?

tf.s: The National Trust is one of the UK's largest charities.
